ctr_personnel.name: Artifacts do not provide enough information to understand the scope of work contained within the WBS Control Accounts. While near-term scope is detailed inside Jira, program leadership must have high-level scope clarity directly within the baseline planning artifacts rather than being forced to search through execution-level tools. The movement of work packages between control accounts opens the door for deliverables to become misplaced and scope boundaries to become vague.

data.leadership_messages: The contractor has established a conceptually sound planning hierarchy and logical workflows; the framework remains largely unpopulated. The ambiguity in Control Account scope prevents the government from digesting theoretical planning into an executable, resource-loaded Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) that tracks earned value.
data.rationale: Cross integration is immature and was not presented in any discernable way at this point in time. Further meetings are necessary to understand the contractor’s theoretical process for incorporating integration and testing tasks into the WBS architecture.

areas.text: WP Rollup IIR2, Sentinel EMD WBS Dictionary, and WBS_RAM (all pulled from NG Extranet 08/05/2026)

S-1 (Task Decomposition): The contractor has successfully decomposed the high-level scope into a list of WPs/PPs within the RAM, providing a logical foundation for future planning if and when evidence is provided.

Follow Up 1: P – 2 (Planning Structure and Task Definition Maturity) Information Gap: The organizational boundaries and tracking mechanisms for cross-IPT Control Accounts are undefined. Action Needed: Request the contractor deliver a Control Account / IPT Mapping Matrix and a process demonstration showing how they intend to isolate, track, and report progress for work within a single Control Account that is actively being executed by multiple distinct engineering teams. Follow Up 2: P – 2 (Planning Structure and Task Definition Maturity) The contractor asserts that detailed plans exist within the P6 scheduling tool, but no evidence has been provided to the Government for review. The Government requires read-only access to, or regularly scheduled demonstrations of, the current P6 schedule for this control account. This is necessary to substantiate planning maturity and to enable evidence-based, rather than trust-based, oversight.
